why: With at most 10 pizzas and 10 toppings there are only 10 * (1 + 10 + 45) orders, so brute-force enumeration is optimal. The week's binary-search idea is the scalable version: sort all topping sums and binary search for x - pizza; here it is not needed.
hints: Count the possible orders: one pizza times (no topping, one topping, or a pair of different toppings).
List all topping extras (0, each single, each distinct pair), then try every pizza + extra and keep the one closest to x, preferring the cheaper on ties.
O(n * m^2) = about 560 checks. For large inputs: sort the extras and binary search for x - pizza.
pitfalls: A topping cannot be used twice: pairs are i < j only (example 4).
Ties in distance go to the lower price (900 beats 1100 for x = 1000).
m can be 0: the only extra is 0.
